clue.text: Admonisher unexpectedly reconciled

indicators.note: something done unexpectedly comes out in a surprising form, so the letters of the word before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scolding person surprisingly makes peace with someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admonisher' looks like the subject of the sentence, but its ten letters are the anagram fodder, rearranged under 'unexpectedly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Differences that have been reconciled are brought into agreement, made to sit together in harmony.

clue.text: Trouble with stern on vessel

parts.note: a stern manner is a hard one
a ship is a seagoing vessel

explanation.surface: Something goes wrong at the back of a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stern' suggests the rear of a boat beside 'vessel', but here it is the adjective meaning severe.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouble in the sense of suffering or adversity is a synonym for privation and difficulty.

clue.text: Rogue crashed cars going over a lake

indicators.note: cars that have crashed are mangled, so the letters of the word are scrambled

parts.note: L is the standard map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A villain wrecks cars that then plunge over into a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' rearranges CARS into RASC; in a down clue 'going over' places it above A and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A rogue is a dishonest or mischievous person, a scamp or scoundrel.

clue.text: Men supporting old renegade, one who makes speeches

indicators.note: in a down clue, a piece supporting another sits below it, so the soldiers come last

parts.note: a rat is someone who deserts their side, a renegade
OR stands for other ranks, the ordinary soldiers or men in the army

explanation.surface: Soldiers back an elderly turncoat who gives speeches.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who makes speeches, especially formal and eloquent ones, is a public speaker.

clue.text: Popular English stage worker lacking in good taste

parts.note: something popular is in, fashionable
a leg is a stage of a journey or race
the worker ant is the crossword's favourite worker

explanation.surface: A well-liked English theatre hand turns out to have no taste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage worker' reads as a stagehand in the theatre, but the two words must be clued separately.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelegant describes something clumsy or graceless, without refinement or good taste.

clue.text: Struggle for supremacy of pair of boxers maybe

definitions.meaning: a fierce contest for dominance between rivals, as between air pilots
a fight between two dogs, boxers being a dog breed

explanation.surface: A bout between two fighters to settle who is top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxers' suggests prize-fighters, but here they are the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitter contest for dominance, and literally a scrap between two dogs such as boxers.

clue.text: Third note followed by second note

indicators.note: the first piece comes before, followed by the next in order

parts.note: me (or mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A musical scale is being recited note by note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' first means a musical note, then a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: A short written note passed round an office is a memorandum.

clue.text: Person making proposal involving source of metal as a further matter

indicators.note: involving means taking something in, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a mover is someone who proposes a motion
ore is the rock metal is extracted from

explanation.surface: A proposer at a meeting brings up mining as an additional point.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb introduces an extra point, meaning besides or in addition to what has been said.

clue.text: Fascinating spells describing web?

indicators.note: describing in the sense of drawing a line around, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: magic is what spells work
a net is a web of mesh

explanation.surface: Someone finds spells cast over the internet fascinating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometric sense, to trace a line round something, which is why it signals one piece enclosing another.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnetic personality attracts and charms people, holding their attention.

clue.text: Phrase badly: editor changed again

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A clumsy sentence has been reworked by an editor.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reshaped has been given a new form, altered once more.

clue.text: Bishop leaves trash in this place for housing vehicles

indicators.note: when the letter leaves it departs, so it is taken out of the word

parts.note: garbage is trash, rubbish
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A clergyman dumps his rubbish in the car shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A garage is a building where cars and other motor vehicles are kept.

clue.text: Dogged son had had a debt

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
taken as written
owed means had a debt to pay

explanation.surface: A boy had run up debts and was persistent about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dogged' looks like the adjective meaning stubborn, but it is the verb: followed closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To be dogged is to be followed or tailed, just as a detective trails a suspect.

clue.text: Pressed on in anger with Democrat

indicators.note: in places the word before it inside the following piece

parts.note: ire is anger
D is the usual abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: Someone pushed ahead angrily with an American party member.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes that have been pressed have been smoothed flat with a hot iron.

clue.text: Crafty part of researches

indicators.note: part of means only some of the letters of the word are taken, a run inside it

explanation.surface: Some of a study shows cunning.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch means knowingly mischievous or sly, as in an arch smile.

clue.text: Ingenuous, worried examinee

parts.note: ingenuous means frank and open, candid
ate means worried or troubled, as in what's eating you?

explanation.surface: A naive person is anxious before a test.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' gives ATE through the idiom of something eating at you.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate is someone sitting an examination.

clue.text: Essential constituent of diet for one in ten

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

indicators.note: in puts the piece before it inside the one that follows

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A dietary staple suits one person in every ten.
explanation.definitionFit: Protein is a nutrient the body needs, a vital part of what we eat.

clue.text: Poison that could make ten Arabs unwell

indicators.note: letters that are unwell are out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A toxin capable of making a group of ten people ill.
explanation.definitionFit: Ratsbane is an old name for rat poison, especially arsenic.

clue.text: The rates adjusted in drama venues

indicators.note: letters that are adjusted are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: Playhouses' local taxes have been changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rates' were British local property taxes, which venues would pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Playhouses are buildings where plays and other dramatic works are staged.

clue.text: Lonely single very excited to go topless

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral one, means single
so means very, as in so happy

indicators.note: topless means without its top, so the first letter goes from the word

parts.note: elated means excited and joyful

explanation.surface: A single person is lonely, but thrilled to strip off their top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go topless' takes the first letter E off ELATED, leaving LATED.
explanation.definitionFit: Being isolated means being cut off from others, alone and remote.

clue.text: Environs of ancient area of land captivate

indicators.note: environs are the surroundings, so only the outside letters of the word are kept

parts.note: a tract is an expanse of land

explanation.surface: The surroundings of an old piece of territory are enchanting.
explanation.definitionFit: To captivate someone is to draw them in, charm or allure them.

clue.text: Trains regularly covered by ticket sellers for holidaymakers

indicators.note: a piece covered by another is wrapped inside it

parts.note: touts sell tickets unofficially, often at inflated prices

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers find train tickets sold by touts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second, fourth and sixth letters of Trains; 'Trains' is fodder, not railways.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourists are people travelling for pleasure, sightseers on holiday.

clue.text: Astound enthusiasts heading west

indicators.note: in an across clue, heading west means reading right to left, so the word is reversed

parts.note: nuts are enthusiasts, as in golf nuts

explanation.surface: Fans travel westward and amaze everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to shock or amaze them, leaving them speechless.

clue.text: Singular repugnance for reactive element

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
odium is hatred or disgust, repugnance

explanation.surface: A unique loathing for a volatile chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodium is a soft alkali metal that reacts violently with water.

clue.text: We hear member of cathedral staff is a great gun

indicators.note: we hear means the clue word is said aloud and spelt another way

parts.note: a canon is a clergyman on a cathedral chapter

explanation.surface: Someone praises a clergyman as a great guy.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannon is a large heavy piece of artillery.

clue.text: Severely criticise a small journey at sea?

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
a sail is a trip on a boat

explanation.surface: Someone slates a short boat trip.
explanation.definitionFit: To assail someone is to attack them vigorously, here with words.

clue.text: Underage person grasping cross bullish monster

indicators.note: grasping means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a minor is someone under legal age
a tau is a T-shaped cross

explanation.surface: A child clutches a crucifix against a frightening beast.
explanation.definitionFit: The Minotaur of Greek myth had a bull's head on a man's body.

clue.text: Exotic raptor bird

indicators.note: exotic means strange and outlandish, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A foreign bird of prey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raptor bird' reads as one phrase, but raptor is only the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A parrot is a brightly coloured tropical bird known for mimicry.

clue.text: Different forms of volume and notes from time to time limiting melody

indicators.note: limiting means bounding on either side, so the pieces surround the other
from time to time means only every other letter of the word is used

parts.note: an aria is a solo melody in opera

explanation.surface: A music book and its occasional notes keep a tune in various versions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from time to time' takes NTS from notes; V and NTS together bound ARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Variants are versions of something that differ slightly from one another.

clue.text: International leaves footballer in difficulty

indicators.note: when the letter leaves the name it is taken out of it

parts.note: Lionel Messi is the Argentine football star

explanation.surface: A footballer quits his national team and finds himself in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'International' looks like a sporting cap, but gives only its abbreviation I.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a mess means being in a fix, a troublesome situation.

clue.text: Resolves to prevent explosive devices

parts.note: to deter is to discourage or prevent
mines are buried explosive devices

explanation.surface: Someone decides to stop bombs.
explanation.definitionFit: To decide or settle a matter is to resolve it, fix it firmly.
